cases.purpose: killall matches NAME against comm exactly (similar names untouched), unions multiple and duplicate NAMEs once, matches over-15-byte names, never signals the shell, defaults to SIGTERM and reports 'no process found' with status 1.
cases.oracle: psmisc 23.7 killall run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of stdout, stderr (location prefix normalized) and status; children are owned fixture processes (symlinks of sleep with unique names) and their end states are read back with kill -0 / wait status.

cases.purpose: killall delivers exactly one signal to a uniquely named direct child, whose pid, parent, uid and comm are verified from /proc just before delivery; the child is then reaped and nothing stray remains.
cases.oracle: psmisc 23.7 killall run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes

cases.purpose: killall -u with a numeric UID selects by real UID and a nonmatching UID selects nothing with status 1 even when NAME matches; an unknown account name selects nothing.
cases.oracle: Requirement text plus kernel facts about the owned fixture processes (kill -0 liveness, /proc/PID/status Uid/PPid/Name); psmisc 23.7 killall has no -f and resolves -u only by account name, so it cannot serve as a reference for these forms.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and the fixture's own /proc facts; no reference tool takes part.
cases.stdout:
nonmatch rc=1
state: x=alive
badname rc-nonzero=yes
state: x=alive
numeric rc=0
state: x=dead

cases.purpose: killall -f matches the space-joined full command line exactly: a substring does not match, the exact line does, and only the matching process is signalled.

cases.stdout:
